observation: Round 1 was a null result: proxy 0.6098 -> 0.6094, sam_fill_rate bit-identical (0.7561778560970978), correspondence_f1@15 0.3162 -> 0.3159, and the prompt set is unchanged (2 positive_slope, 6 midpoint, 2 assume at the same coordinates). Relaxing the oblique Hough path (50->35, gap 50->70) and binarisation (127->110) therefore did not change stage-4 output; the only measurable effect was the curvature nudge raising depth_nan_ratio 0.193 -> 0.194. Re-reading the round-1 artifacts pixel-precisely (detected_lines.png calibrated on the 10 ring verticals at x=180+360k, initial_prompt_points.png on its grid) shows that the 6 'midpoint' prompts are K-block centres taken as the midpoint of a positive-slope (top) and negative-slope (bottom) oblique intersection, not horizontal fallbacks. Anchoring the design pattern (K=245.4 px, AB=745.4 px, circumference 4712 px = depth-map height) at each prompt and comparing with the horizontal Hough joints in that ring gives: rings 1260, 1980, 2700, 3060, 3420 within |6| px (correct); ring 1620 consistently +13..+25 px; ring 2340 consistently -20..-24 px; assume ring 900 -55..-60 px. In rings 1620 and 2340 the K centre was formed from a spurious short oblique segment (~190 px, 7.5-8.1 deg; e.g. green at y~2220 in ring 1620, red at y~1315 in ring 2340) instead of the true K edge (~350 px, 9.0-9.2 deg; y~2262 and y~1266 respectively). The spurious pairings have a red-green separation of 188-208 px (37-57 px off the K prior), whereas true pairs measure 252-255 px (7-10 px off the prior). Single-edge rings 540 and 3060 rely on 136-173 px red lines, shorter than the spurious segments, so raising the oblique Hough threshold would remove the genuine edges before the spurious ones.
